problem.headline: Building a Startup Is Still a Black Box
problem.summary: Founders spend weeks assembling pitch decks, writing technical specs, and planning sprints manually — tasks that should take minutes, not months. Non-technical founders are locked out of architecture decisions, and technical founders waste time on business strategy docs instead of building.
pain_points: Founders waste 40+ hours creating pitch decks and PRDs before writing a single line of code
Non-technical founders cannot evaluate architecture recommendations without expensive consultants
Sprint planning is ad-hoc and inconsistent, leading to scope creep and missed deadlines
Existing tools (Notion, Jira, Google Slides) are disconnected — no single source of truth
Hackathon teams lose 30% of their time on planning instead of building

solution.headline: From Idea to Execution-Ready Blueprint in 3 Minutes
solution.summary: Orchestra uses 5 specialized AI agents working in parallel to transform a plain-text idea into a complete startup blueprint — covering architecture, wireframes, pitch deck, documentation, and sprint planning. One input, five expert outputs, zero guesswork.
key_features: Multi-agent AI orchestration with parallel execution for speed
Professional-grade pitch deck content with market analysis and GTM strategy
Tailored technical architecture recommendations with system topology diagrams
Sprint-level project plans with milestones, team roles, and deliverables
One-click section regeneration to iterate without starting over

market.market_size: $18.2 billion Total Addressable Market — spanning project management ($7.2B), AI developer tools ($5.8B), and pitch deck / startup tools ($5.2B). Growing at 24% CAGR driven by AI adoption.
target_users: Early-stage startup founders (pre-seed to Series A) — 5.4 million new startups globally per year
Product managers at growth-stage companies needing rapid feature scoping
Hackathon participants (2 million+ annually) needing fast project planning
Indie hackers and solopreneurs building side projects
Startup accelerators and incubators running cohort programs
trends: AI-native development tools replacing manual workflows (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, v0)
Rise of solo founders and micro-SaaS — 40% of Y Combinator S24 batch were solo founders
Shift from monolithic planning tools to AI-generated, context-aware outputs
Growing demand for instant, investor-ready materials in competitive fundraising markets

revenue_streams: Freemium SaaS — 3 free generations/month, unlimited on Pro ($19/mo) and Team ($49/mo/seat)
Enterprise licenses for accelerators and incubators ($499/mo for cohort access)
API access for integration into existing developer workflows ($0.10 per generation)
Premium templates and industry-specific agent configurations
business_model.pricing: Freemium model with generous free tier to drive adoption. Pro tier at $19/month unlocks unlimited generations, export features, and team sharing. Enterprise tier at $499/month includes custom agents, SSO, and priority support.

channels: Product Hunt launch targeting #1 Product of the Day
Developer community seeding on Twitter/X, Reddit r/startups, Hacker News
Content marketing — 'From Idea to Blueprint' YouTube series and blog
Startup accelerator partnerships (Y Combinator, Techstars, 500 Global)
go_to_market.acquisition_strategy: Product-led growth with a viral sharing loop — every generated blueprint includes a 'Powered by Orchestra' watermark. Target 1,000 free users in first month via Product Hunt + Hacker News launch, convert 8% to paid within 90 days.

roadmap.phase_1: MVP Launch (Month 1-2): 5-agent blueprint generation, web dashboard, basic auth. Target: 500 beta users, validate core value proposition with NPS > 40.
roadmap.phase_2: Growth (Month 3-6): Team collaboration features, PDF/Notion export, custom agent tuning, API access. Target: 5,000 users, $10K MRR, raise pre-seed.
roadmap.phase_3: Scale (Month 7-12): Enterprise features (SSO, audit logs), marketplace for community agents, mobile app, real-time collaboration. Target: 25,000 users, $100K MRR.

suggestions.title: Launch at a Major Hackathon First
suggestions.description: Use a hackathon demo as the initial proof of concept. Hackathon participants are the ideal early adopter — they need fast planning, they're tech-savvy, and they share tools virally. A successful hackathon demo creates immediate credibility and a user base.

suggestions.title: Build Export Integrations Early
suggestions.description: Users will want to take their blueprints into existing tools (Notion, Jira, Linear, Google Slides). Building export integrations in Phase 2 dramatically increases stickiness and bridges the gap between planning and execution.

suggestions.title: Create Industry-Specific Agent Templates
suggestions.description: Pre-trained agent configurations for common startup verticals (SaaS, marketplace, fintech, healthtech) will significantly improve output quality and reduce the need for prompt engineering by end users.

suggestions.title: Implement a 'Blueprint Score' Metric
suggestions.description: Add a completeness and quality score to each generated blueprint. This gamifies the experience, encourages regeneration of weak sections, and provides a benchmark that users can share — driving word-of-mouth growth.
